extracted.intended_audience: new and prospective contributors to the SymPy open-source project
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for new contributors on how to get started contributing code, documentation, reviews, and community help to the SymPy project using the project's workflows and etiquette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get familiar using the software
rubrics_metrics.description: We suggest going through the SymPy Tutorial to get acquainted with using the software before you begin contributing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing the tutorial helps you familiarize yourself with the uses of SymPy; the tutorial is also available in video form (links provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the 2017 SymPy paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the authored 2017 journal paper that provides a high-level look at SymPy and its capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper (linked) gives context and a high-level overview useful before contributing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peruse the documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse the documentation to get an idea of available topics and functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the tutorial, there is a lot of information in the docs; skimming topics helps you learn what's already covered and where contributions may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants in the SymPy community are expected to abide by our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the Code of Conduct before getting started to understand expected community behavior and norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join and use the mailing list with etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Join the SymPy email mailing list to ask questions, discuss feature requests, bugs, usage, and share how you use SymPy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request to join on Google Groups; first-time posts are moderated to prevent spam. Read the recommended mailing list etiquette (linked PDF) before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up your development environment (use Git and GitHub)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Git for version control and GitHub as the web interface for communication, issue tracking, and merging contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new to Git/GitHub, read the 'Setup Development Environment' page for instructions on configuring your environment and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the SymPy development workflow on GitHub
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the GitHub contribution workflow aspects that are specific to SymPy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If already familiar with basic GitHub workflows, read the 'Development Workflow Process' page to learn SymPy-specific procedures for issues, pull requests, and merging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify something meaningful to work on
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose from many contribution types: fixing bugs, adding new features, maintaining websites, writing documentation, preparing tutorials, answering questions, and reviewing pull requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To start with the main codebase, look for issues labeled 'Easy to fix' in the issue tracker. If it isn’t clear how to fix an issue, ask for suggestions in the issue or on the mailing list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the SymPy codebase organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Know that SymPy's code is organized into Python packages and modules (e.g., sympy/core for core code; other packages like sympy/printing handle specific functionality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with the directory layout (sympy/core, sympy/printing, etc.) helps you locate where to implement fixes or features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to documentation correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: SymPy documentation lives in two places: documentation source files (doc/src) and the docstrings in the source code; both are shown on the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can click the '[Source]' link next to function docs to jump to the docstring. Every function/class has a docstring explaining use (shown via help(function_name)). While contributing to docs, follow the SymPy Documentation Style Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review pull requests before merges
rubrics_metrics.description: Every contribution to SymPy goes through a pull request and requires a review before it can be merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you’re familiar with a part of the codebase and the development process, reviewing others’ pull requests is helpful: view the submission and check whether it does what it is intended to do.
